title: Exporting Review Tables to LaTeX
text: reviewTable() can return LaTeX representation summary table inclusion manuscript. Two arguments control LaTeX workflow: latex = TRUE returns table LaTeX code instead gt object. cite = TRUE treats values study ID column BibTeX reference keys wraps row’s study list \cite{...}, citations render correctly document compiled.
code: library(litReview) data(studies)

title: Exporting Review Tables to LaTeX
text: Pass latex = TRUE get LaTeX code:
code: reviewTable(studies, Design, latex = TRUE)

title: Exporting Review Tables to LaTeX
text: StudyID matches keys .bib file (e.g. smith2020, doe2019), set cite = TRUE Studies column wrapped \cite{...}: cite flag also works without latex = TRUE want gt preview cited form:
code: reviewTable(studies, Design, latex = TRUE, cite = TRUE) reviewTable(studies, Design, cite = TRUE, study_id = "bibKey")

what: Embedding in a LaTeX or R Markdown document
title: Exporting Review Tables to LaTeX
text: .Rnw (Sweave) LaTeX-output R Markdown file, use results = "asis" LaTeX code emitted verbatim: Make sure preamble loads citation package (e.g. \usepackage{natbib} \usepackage{biblatex}) keys used StudyID exist bibliography.
code: reviewTable(studies, Design, latex = TRUE, cite = TRUE) \begin{table}[t] \fontsize{12.0pt}{14.0pt}\selectfont \begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}llrr} \toprule Design & Studies & Frequency & Percent \\  \midrule\addlinespace[2.5pt] RCT & \cite{S06,S17,S20,S21,S22,S24,S28,S32,S37,S39,S45} & 11 & 22\% \\  Qualitative & \cite{S01,S03,S08,S18,S33,S35,S38,S43,S49} & 9 & 18\% \\  Mixed methods & \cite{S05,S50} & 2 & 4\% \\  Cross-sectional & \cite{S04,S07,S09,S10,S11,S14,S19,S30,S34,S42,S44,S48} & 12 & 24\% \\  Cohort & \cite{S02,S12,S15,S16,S25,S26,S29,S31,S40,S41,S46,S47} & 12 & 24\% \\  Case-control & \cite{S13,S23,S27,S36} & 4 & 8\% \\  \bottomrule \end{tabular*} \end{table}

title: Exporting Review Tables to LaTeX
text: study IDs live column StudyID, pass via study_id:
code: df <- data.frame(   RefKey = c("smith2020", "doe2019", "lee2021", "smith2020"),   Design = c("RCT", "Cohort", "RCT", "Case-control"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) reviewTable(df, Design, study_id = RefKey, latex = TRUE, cite = TRUE)

title: Getting Started with litReview
text: Literature review datasets often missing values. functions accept na.rm, na_label, na_in_percent control NAs handled. Let’s create example data missing values:
code: df_na <- data.frame(   StudyID = paste0("S", 1:10),   Design  = c("RCT", "Cohort", NA, "RCT", "Case-control",               NA, "RCT", "Cohort", NA, "RCT"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )

title: Getting Started with litReview
text: NAs dropped, denominator 10 studies. Percentages reflect share full sample, sum 100%:
code: summarize_data(df_na, Design) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   Design       Studies         Frequency Percent #>   <chr>        <chr>               <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Case-control S5                      1      10 #> 2 Cohort       S2, S8                  2      20 #> 3 RCT          S1, S4, S7, S10         4      40

what: Drop NAs, percentages of reported only
title: Getting Started with litReview
text: Set na_in_percent = FALSE denominator counts 7 studies reported design. Percentages sum 100%:
code: summarize_data(df_na, Design, na_in_percent = FALSE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   Design       Studies         Frequency Percent #>   <chr>        <chr>               <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Case-control S5                      1    14.3 #> 2 Cohort       S2, S8                  2    28.6 #> 3 RCT          S1, S4, S7, S10         4    57.1

title: Getting Started with litReview
text: Set na.rm = FALSE include “reported” category. percentages sum 100%:
code: summarize_data(df_na, Design, na.rm = FALSE) #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   Design       Studies         Frequency Percent #>   <chr>        <chr>               <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Case-control S5                      1      10 #> 2 Cohort       S2, S8                  2      20 #> 3 Not reported S3, S6, S9              3      30 #> 4 RCT          S1, S4, S7, S10         4      40

what: Keep NAs with a custom label, percentages of reported
title: Getting Started with litReview
text: Combine three parameters. “Missing” replaces NA, denominator excludes missing rows:
code: summarize_data(df_na, Design, na.rm = FALSE, na_label = "Missing",                na_in_percent = FALSE) #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   Design       Studies         Frequency Percent #>   <chr>        <chr>               <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Case-control S5                      1    14.3 #> 2 Cohort       S2, S8                  2    28.6 #> 3 Missing      S3, S6, S9              3    42.9 #> 4 RCT          S1, S4, S7, S10         4    57.1

title: litReview: Summarizing Graphs for Literature Reviews — litReview-package
text: Provides functions summarize visualize categorical data literature reviews. Generates bar charts, waffle charts, donut plots, co-occurrence heatmaps, trend charts, world maps reporting study characteristics across multiple publications.

text: Maintainer: Sonsoles López-Pernas sonsoles.lopez@uef.fi Authors: Kamila Misiejuk Mohammed Saqr

title: Create an Alluvial (Sankey) Plot — reviewAlluvial
text: Shows co-occurrence flow categories across multiple columns. study traces path strata. Requires ggalluvial package.

title: Create an Alluvial (Sankey) Plot — reviewAlluvial
code: reviewAlluvial(   data,   cols,   sep = "\r\n",   study_id = StudyID,   colors = PALETTE,   base_size = 12,   na.rm = TRUE,   na_label = "Not reported",   labels = c("none", "prop", "count", "both"),   flow_labels = FALSE,   flow_alpha = 0.25,   stratum_width = 0.5,   axis_labels = NULL )

title: Create an Alluvial (Sankey) Plot — reviewAlluvial
text: data data frame. cols Character vector column names use axes (left right). sep Character. Separator multi-value cells. Defaults "\r\n". column contains multi-value cells, combination generates separate alluvium. study_id Column containing study identifiers (quoted unquoted). Defaults StudyID. colors Character vector. Fill colors strata, cycled matched name. Defaults PALETTE. base_size Numeric. Base font size points. Defaults 12. na.rm Logical. Drop rows missing values? Defaults TRUE. na_label Character. Label missing values na.rm = FALSE. Defaults "reported". labels Character. show stratum. One "none" (default), "prop" (proportion within axis), "count", "" (count proportion). flow_labels Logical. TRUE, show counts flows strata. Defaults FALSE. flow_alpha Numeric. Transparency flows (0–1). Defaults 0.25. stratum_width Numeric. Width stratum bars. Defaults 0.5. axis_labels Character vector custom axis labels (length cols), NULL use column names. Defaults NULL.

title: Create an Alluvial (Sankey) Plot — reviewAlluvial
text: ggplot2::ggplot object.

title: Create an Alluvial (Sankey) Plot — reviewAlluvial

title: Create a Summary Bar Chart — reviewBar
text: data data frame least study ID column column named col. col Column visualize (quoted unquoted). fill Character. Bar fill color. Defaults "#7BB0D1". width Numeric. Bar width (0–1). Defaults 0.5. sep Character. Separator multi-value cells. Defaults "\r\n". studlabs Logical. TRUE, draws study ID labels bars using ggfittext::geom_bar_text(). Defaults FALSE. study_id Column containing study identifiers (quoted unquoted). Defaults StudyID. label_space Numeric. Multiplier x-axis headroom fit labels. Defaults 1.6. base_size Numeric. Base font size points; controls proportional scaling text elements. Defaults 12. na.rm Logical. Drop missing values? Defaults TRUE. na_label Character. Label missing values na.rm = FALSE. Defaults "reported". na_in_percent Logical. Include missing rows percentage denominator? Defaults TRUE. na_last Logical. TRUE, place missing-value category last regardless frequency. Defaults FALSE.

title: Create a Year-Trend Bar Chart — reviewTrend
text: data data frame least StudyID (column set study_id), column named col, year column. col Column visualize (quoted unquoted). year_col Year column (quoted unquoted). Defaults Year. sep Character. Reference Full reference string. Country Country countries study conducted. Multi-value cells separated newlines. Design Study design (e.g. RCT, Cohort, Cross-sectional). SampleSize Number participants. FollowUpWeeks Follow-duration weeks, NA. AgeGroup Target age group. May contain multiple values. Setting Study setting (e.g. Hospital, Community, Online). Intervention Intervention type (e.g. CBT, Exercise). May contain multiple values. Outcome Reported outcome (e.g. Pain, Function). May contain multiple values. AnalysisApproach Statistical analytical approach used. RiskOfBias Risk bias rating (Low, Moderate, High, NA). FundingSource Funding source, NA. OpenAccess Whether study open access (Yes, , NA). what: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
title: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
text: Splits multi-value cells, counts frequencies, computes percentages.

title: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
code: summarize_data(   data,   col,   sep = "\r\n",   study_id = StudyID,   na.rm = TRUE,   na_label = "Not reported",   na_in_percent = TRUE,   na_last = FALSE )

title: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
text: data data frame containing least columns specified col study_id. col Column summarize (quoted unquoted). sep Character. separator used split multi-value cells. Defaults "\r\n". study_id Column containing study identifiers (quoted unquoted). Defaults StudyID. na.rm Logical. TRUE (default), rows missing values (NA empty strings) col dropped. FALSE, kept labelled na_label. na_label Character. Label used missing values na.rm = FALSE. Defaults "reported". na_in_percent Logical. TRUE (default), denominator percentages total number rows (including missing). FALSE, non-missing rows counted, non-missing categories sum \(\approx 100\%\). na_last Logical. TRUE, missing-value row (na.rm = FALSE) placed bottom result regardless frequency. Defaults FALSE (sorted frequency like rows).

title: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
text: data frame columns grouping variable, Studies (comma-separated study IDs), Frequency, Percent (numeric, 0–100).

title: Summarize Frequency of Values in a Column — summarize_data
code: df <- data.frame(   StudyID = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"),   Design = c("RCT", "Cohort", NA, "RCT"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Drop NAs (default) summarize_data(df, Design) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   Design Studies Frequency Percent #>   <chr>  <chr>       <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Cohort S2              1      25 #> 2 RCT    S1, S4          2      50  # Keep NAs with a custom label summarize_data(df, Design, na.rm = FALSE, na_label = "Missing") #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   Design  Studies Frequency Percent #>   <chr>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Missing S3              1      25 #> 2 Cohort  S2              1      25 #> 3 RCT     S1, S4          2      50  # Percentages of non-missing only summarize_data(df, Design, na_in_percent = FALSE) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   Design Studies Frequency Percent #>   <chr>  <chr>       <int>   <dbl> #> 1 Cohort S2              1    33.3 #> 2 RCT    S1, S4          2    66.7
